name: PA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Brendan Boyle with large cash advantage
Republican challenger with no fundraising or polling presence
model.rationale: Boyle is a well-funded incumbent in a D+19 Philadelphia district, while Arriaga shows no measurable fundraising or campaign infrastructure. Fundamentals point to a blowout, and prediction markets agree the seat is effectively out of play.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or Boyle's unexpected withdrawal would put this seat in question.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 2nd District is a heavily Democratic Philadelphia-area seat, and Brendan Boyle is running for reelection with a dominant financial position: over $2.4 million raised and $5.5 million on hand, with no outside opposition spending. His Republican challenger, Jessica Arriaga, reports no fundraising and has no visible campaign operation.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but the district's D+19 partisan lean, Boyle's incumbency, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win around 94% all point the same way. The forecast expects Boyle to win by roughly 25 points, consistent with recent district performance, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-attention race.
